properties.location: Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham
properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham.

  • Upstream flows from the Murray River, combined with floodwaters from the Goulburn River, may cause minor flooding along the Murray River at Barham from as early as Thursday. 
  • The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.30m and steady, below the minor flood level and may exceed 5.50m from Thursday 20 August, with minor flooding.
  • Further rises are expected as upstream flows approach Barham next week.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater. 
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Camping grounds may be flooded.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 19/08/2026 03:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for parts of the Goulburn River downstream of Shepparton. 

Minor flooding is possible along the Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge.

Along the Goulburn River, river level rises are occurring at McCoys Bridge as upstream flood water arrives. Renewed river level rises are possible along the Goulburn River with forecast rainfall during later Tuesday and Wednesday.
The situation is being closely monitored and this warning will be updated as required.

The Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge is currently at 8.75 m and steady, below the minor flood level. The Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge may peak near the minor flood level (9.00 m) during Wednesday.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • People living or camping on the Goulburn River between Shepparton and Kanyapella should expect river level rises as floodwater arrives from Shepparton. 
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery from along the river to higher ground. 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Monitor river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge at Bandiana.

Minor flooding is possible along the Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge.

Minor flooding has eased along the Kiewa River at Bandiana, however river levels remain elevated along the Kiewa River in response to recent rainfall.
Further rainfall is forecast across the catchment for the next few days, which may cause renewed river level rises.

The situation is being closely monitored and this warning will be updated as necessary.

The Kiewa River at Bandiana is currently at 2.77 m and steady, below the minor flood level. Renewed river level rises to the minor flood level (2.80 m) is possible along the Kiewa River at Bandiana from Wednesday evening.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation.
Impacts in your area: 
  • For the latest road closures go to the VicTraffic website.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Loddon River, Loddon Weir to Kerang.

MINOR FLOODING OCCURRING AT APPIN SOUTH

Along the Loddon River at Appin South the river level is approaching a minor peak.

Renewed river level rises are possible along the Loddon River with forecast rainfall during later Tuesday and Wednesday. 

Forecast rain from Tuesday evening onwards may see renewed river rises within the catchment, but impacts are not currently expected to exceed the rainfall event last week.

The situation is being closely monitored and this warning will be updated as required.
 
Loddon River Loddon Weir to Kerang:

Minor flooding is occurring at Appin South.

The Loddon River at Appin South is currently at 2.98 m and steady, with minor flooding. 

The Loddon River at Appin South may peak near 3.00 m overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, with minor flooding. 

Further rises are possible with forecast rainfall.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and be prepared to act if your situation changes.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwaters
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Over-floor flooding of dwellings is not currently expected. 
  • Impacts expected to be limited to inundation of lower areas of Loddon floodplain with possible inundation of some minor local roads.
  • Roads and bridges may be closed due to flooding.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 19/08/2026 01:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Winds are expected to ease during the afternoon....
